Product history

From a single training need to a country-aware platform.

Aerobridge began with Aviation English, then grew into a platform that separates shared aviation knowledge from national requirements.

The change

Aerobridge outgrew a one-course website.

Aviation English remained important, but learners also needed theory, practice, progress and authority requirements in one place.

Foundation

Aviation English preparation

The original focus was operational English and preparation for ICAO language proficiency.

Platform rebuild

Training became a product

Lessons, practice, progress, resources and requirements moved into a dedicated learner platform.

Shared core

Pilot theory expanded the catalog

The new program introduced an ICAO-aligned knowledge spine with national references kept separate.

Country layer

Chile became the first active pack

DGAC licensing, medical, examination and practical references were organised as versioned source records.

Next phase

Expansion follows verification

Additional programs and country packs remain planned until their curriculum, sources and pathways are ready.

Why the model changed

International does not mean identical.

The underlying aviation knowledge can be shared, but licence paths, medical rules, approved exams and source documents change by authority. Aerobridge is structured around that reality.
